rule: Every AWS CLI action a recipe may run under the runner is listed here by hand, with the IAM action(s) it needs and one line on why it does not mutate the account. Admission is a code-reviewed change to this file; nothing is admitted by verb pattern — `start`, `generate` and `validate` appear below because a reviewer read what each does, and `Describe*` appears entry by entry for the same reason. An action absent from both lists is unknown, and a recipe using one is manual until it is reviewed. `refused` names the actions the pinned recipes use that the runner will never run, with the reason. `runner` names the two calls the runner makes on its own behalf.

refused.why: runs a query whose results Athena writes to an S3 output location. It writes into the account, and the runner writes nothing. Refused; `audit-reduction-and-report-generation` is manual for this and its CloudTrail Lake alternative is what the runner may use.

writes a CycloneDX SBOM into an S3 bucket under a KMS key — `--s3-destination bucketName=…,keyPrefix=…`. It is an export job that puts objects into the account, and the runner puts nothing anywhere. Refused; `acquisition-scanning-and-sbom-inventory` is manual for it, and the SBOM belongs in the pipeline plane's evidence where the commit anchors it.

executes a document — with AWS-RunShellScript, an arbitrary shell command — on the targeted instances. The one recipe using it (`clock-synchronization-and-timestamps`) runs `chronyc` on production-tagged hosts. Refused outright; the recipe is manual.

runner.why: the runner's own: which principal, in which account, is making these calls — recorded in every transcript. Always permitted; it cannot be denied by policy.
the runner's own self-check (T3-3): simulates a probe set of mutating actions against its own role and refuses to run unless every one is denied. Evaluates policies; changes none.
